newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Commerce Chamber's Christie to leave end April.
newsitem.headline: HK Commerce Chamber's Christie to leave end April.

text.p: Ian Christie, director of the Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce, will leave the chamber on April 30, chairman James Tien said in a statement on Tuesday.
Christie will be replaced by China expert Eden Woon, executive director of the Washington State China Relations Council in the United States, the statement said.
Woon, a former China policy advisor for the U.S. Secretary for Defence, will take up his new position on May 19.
Christie, 61, almost nine years in the chamber, said it was appropriate now to localise the post as Hong Kong's transfer to China draws close.

"It's appropriate at this time to localise the post in order to find someone who is fluent in Putonghua (Chinese) in view of the increasingly close relationship...of Hong Kong and China," Christie told Reuters.
Hong Kong, a British colony of over 150 years, reverts to China at midnight June 30. Vestiges of British colonialism are fading in the approach of the handover.
Christie said his departure would not affect the key role of the chamber, that of promoting, representing and safeguarding the interests of all its members, Chinese and non-Chinese alike.
"The chamber is an international chamber of commerce. That is its strength and that is its future, a go-between link between China and the West in all terms," Christie said.
